title: Module Assessment & Fable Showcase
description: Synthesize and demonstrate mastery of fable elements and figurative language including personification, similes, metaphors, hyperbole, and moral extraction.

components.content:
### Welcome to the Module Assessment!

Throughout this module, you have learned the key components of traditional fables and analyzed powerful literary techniques used by authors to bring animal characters to life and convey timeless morals.

Now, test your knowledge across personification, similes, metaphors, hyperbole, onomatopoeia, and moral analysis!

components.title: Module Concepts Summary Table
data: Gives human traits to animals or objects
The wind sang a gentle lullaby.
He ran as fast as a cheetah.
States that one thing IS another
Her heart was a fortress of strength.
I've waited in line for a thousand years!
A word that mimics a natural sound
CRASH! The vase shattered on the floor.

components.content:
### Identifying Devices in Context

Read each sentence carefully. Ask yourself whether the sentence is making a comparison, exaggerating a trait, imitating a sound, or giving human actions to non-human entities.

components.title: Identify the Device Used
components.text:
1. 'The owl whispered wisdom to the forest.' uses {{blank}}.
2. 'The mouse was as quiet as a falling feather.' uses a {{blank}}.
3. 'The fox's tail was a flame in the dark.' uses a {{blank}}.

slides.subtitle: Analyze The Town Mouse and The Country Mouse

components.title: Tap the Hotspots to Analyze Fable Elements

hotspots.label: Country Life (Simile)
hotspots.content: Description: 'The country mouse lived as simple as a sparrow.' (Compares humble lifestyle using 'as').

hotspots.label: Town Feast (Hyperbole)
hotspots.content: Description: 'The town feast contained a million delicious delicacies!' (Exaggerates the luxury).

hotspots.label: The Moral
hotspots.content: Moral: 'A humble life in peace and safety is far better than luxury accompanied by fear.'

slides.title: Final Module Assessment Quiz
slides.subtitle: Prove Your Fables & Figurative Language Mastery

questions.question: Which sentence contains BOTH personification and onomatopoeia?
options: The bird flew high into the blue sky.
SQUEAK! The wooden floorboards groaned under the bear's heavy footsteps.
The tortoise was slower than a snail on a cold morning.
The fox was a sneaky bandit.
questions.explanation: 'SQUEAK!' is onomatopoeia and floorboards 'groaned' is personification.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a fable?
options: To list real historical facts about ancient Greece.
To entertain readers while teaching a clear moral or life lesson.
To teach science facts about animal diets.
To explain how to draw wild animals.
questions.explanation: Fables combine engaging animal stories with practical moral instruction.
